propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark calls author() 6,000 times, each invoking git config user.name via subprocess, consuming 47.79s of the 77-108s total import time
Each CREATE ticket in the import triggers sweep_stale_staging, causing 3,000 redundant sweeps and 375,876 staging-owner checks despite identical staging root across a batch, consuming 15.94s
Introducing an explicit contextvar-scoped author cache for import context eliminates redundant git config reads while preserving live per-call lookup for interactive writes

Deferring stale-staging sweep to the first new ticket per batch (via sweep_stale parameter) eliminates 2,988 redundant sweeps per import while preserving sweep behavior for direct and interactive callers
Controlled A/B testing with identical state, 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, and 24 commits shows 60.8s (78.8%) wall-time reduction when only git-config and sweep mechanisms are replaced
The optimization must preserve the locked N=3000 contract: 6,000 events, exactly 24 crash-safe commits, >=10x reduction, rollback, and resume capability
